chunks: And from him, from Hammad, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the charity of alms-giving at the breaking of the fast (Fitr), he said: 'Give charity on behalf of all those you provide for, whether small or large, free or slave. For every person, half a sa' of wheat, or a sa' of dates, or a sa' of barley. And the sa' is four amdad.'

key_terms.أَمْدَادٍ: A unit of volume measurement (plural of mudd)
key_terms.صَاعٌ: A traditional unit of volume measurement
key_terms.صَدَقَةِ الْفِطْرَةِ: Charity of alms-giving at the breaking of the fast (Zakat al-Fitr)

ai.seo_question: What are the exact quantities and acceptable food types for Zakat al-Fitr according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the foundational fiqh of Zakat al-Fitr, emphasizing the head of household's responsibility to cover all dependents regardless of age or social status. It specifies the standard measure of one sa' (four mudds) for dates or barley, and half a sa' for wheat, reflecting the dietary staples of Medina during the early Islamic period. This ruling underscores the social welfare aspect of the practice, ensuring that the poor can partake in the festive celebrations of Eid. Additionally, it highlights the distinction between the obligatory charity of breaking the fast and the general zakat, anchoring the practice in the Sunnah of the Prophet and the Imams.
